title: Conductivity of a non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid: Exact solution of the kinetic equation
summary: In a Fermi liquid, the quasiparticle scattering rate scales as , whereas the low-temperature correction to the residual resistivity can scale as , seemingly implying a strongly suppressed current-relaxation rate. The authors resolve this paradox here by solving the kinetic equation exactly for a disordered, non-Galilean-invariant Fermi liquid. They show that electron–electron collisions enter the conductivity through the quasiparticle scattering time itself, which controls the crossover between collisionless and hydrodynamic transport. The extra factor arises because momentum conservation makes the change in the total velocity of two colliding electrons vanish on the Fermi surface, so current relaxation comes only from thermally excited states away from it. The electron–electron contribution to the dc conductivity nevertheless remains parametrically small throughout the Fermi-liquid regime. By extrapolating the result toward a quantum critical point, the authors further show that the renormalized quasiparticle scattering rate saturates the Planckian bound.
